grading_system.evidence: Graduation is based upon both credits earned and the demonstration of our Proficiency Based Graduation Requirements.

schedule.evidence: Course listings are marked 'Credits: 1 (Full Year A Day or B Day)' and 'One Semester A Day or B Day'; the number of blocks per day is not stated, so courses_per_term is null. Courses also run one quarter, three quarters, or four quarters.

credit_definition.text: Credits are printed per course: 1 credit for a one-semester course, 2 for a full-year course, .5 for a one-quarter course. Requirements are stated in credits.
credit_definition.evidence: Course #: 01061OW Credits: 1 (One Semester). Course #: 01065HH Credits: .5 (One Quarter). Course #: 01005 Credits: 2 (Full Year).

course_load.min_courses_or_credits: Freshman 8 credits; Sophomore 6; Junior 6; Senior 6; at least three credits per semester
course_load.evidence: All students in grades 9-12 will be enrolled in a minimum of three credits each semester and attend school for a minimum of 5.5 hours excluding lunch.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog already uses credits (1 = one-semester course, 2 = full-year course in its course listings); no conversion needed. Area minimums: English 4, Social Studies 4, Math 3.5, Science 3, PE 1.5, Fine Arts 1, Health 0.5, Service Learning/Internships 0.5, Technology 0.5, World Language 1. The catalog states a traditional 24-credit pathway and separately requires proficiency-based graduation requirements.

flexible_pathways_listed: dual enrollment (CCV / college courses, up to two vouchers)
Burlington Technical Center two-year programs (six high school credits)
Center for Technology Essex full-day programs
notes: Catalog is 2026-27 (76-page PDF). Milton has both a traditional 24-credit pathway and Proficiency Based Graduation Requirements (PBGR); catalog states no proficiency scale or minimum score. Letter grades with a 4.33 GPA scale are used for courses (p.15). Promotion standing requires 6 (sophomore), 11 (junior) and 17 (senior) credits (p.11). Seniors must complete Service Learning by the end of semester one (sample four-year plan, PAGE 10). Required English 9 and 10; juniors and seniors choose AP or Seminar for English. Math sequence: Algebra I, Geometry, Algebra II and Statistics/AP Stats/Principles of Math. Schedule block count is not stated; the A Day/B Day course markers indicate an A/B schedule. Report card and transcript reflect the Center for Technology Essex grade scale for CTE courses (p.75).
